previous_statement: By lem-maincb-reset-constant-ledger, D_* = max{1,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3}, so D_* >= 1. Applying its global-scalar-call clause at the base scale t := epsilon, using the producer hypotheses from node 1.2.1 and the finite-dimensional extended epsilon-C*-algebra A fixed at the root, yields the literal map u_0(lambda)=lambda I_A furnished by lem-maincb-initial-raw-inclusion as an extended D_*t-inclusion with ||u_0(I_C)-I_A|| <= D_*t, and declares this call eligible for lem-maincb-reset-invariant-preservation.
new_statement: Let D_* = max{1,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3}, as fixed by lem-maincb-reset-constant-ledger, so D_* >= 1. If the additional raw-producer bound t <= e_0 holds, then lem-maincb-initial-raw-inclusion at t := epsilon gives u_0(lambda)=lambda I_A as an extended D_0*t-inclusion; since D_0 <= D_* and t >= 0, the defining error and two-sided norm inequalities weaken to make u_0 an extended D_*t-inclusion. The global-scalar clause of lem-maincb-reset-constant-ledger then gives ||u_0(I_C)-I_A|| <= D_*t and eligibility. However, node 1.2.1 and the allowed external contracts do not establish t <= e_0, so this conditional application does not prove the unconditional conclusion asserted by parent node 1.2.
